findings.text: Per CPU initialization for encrypted guests allocates a table of control block references sized by the global address space identifier count and signals allocation failure, remaining inactive while global support is disabled.

Global teardown for encrypted guests flushes the identifier space, releases tracking bitmaps, clears resource accounting for encrypted flavors, and invokes platform shutdown, remaining inactive while global support is disabled.

Startup publication restricts virtual machine types to firmware supported ones, exposes them through global capability state, announces availability and identifier ranges for each encrypted flavor when the matching processor capability exists, mirrors support flags into enabled flags, and builds the save area feature mask from debug swap and secure timestamp availability plus timer presence.

Reclaim notification for guest memory performs cache maintenance only for legacy encrypted guests, ignoring other guests and secure nested paging guests whose private pages are outside host address based tracking.

Encrypted page maintenance demands a kernel address, uses cache line writeback where coherent encrypted mappings exist, otherwise attempts an identifier tagged page flush with fallback to full cache writeback on fault.

Communication block exchange carries a fixed small register set outward on exit and accepts registers plus extended control and privilege state inward only where validity marks allow, while snapshotting validity, propagating exit descriptors into control state, and clearing guest marks after use.

Incoming exit validation universally requires exit descriptors and imposes per category register or scratch demands covering debug, performance, identification with extended state for a specific leaf, string and directional input output, control register access, hypercall with privilege, monitor, wait, processor lifecycle, memory mapped access and page state operations, accepting unlisted categories.

Teardown omits the identifier bitmap lock because no guests survive, and reclaim type checks may run outside the main virtual machine lock because encrypted membership is fixed before virtual CPUs exist and incoherence implies prior execution.
Page state buffer is a tightly packed record with a leading header followed by a flexible trailing sequence of per range entries.

Host mapping release treats empty mappings as success, tears down kernel or memory mapped views, propagates dirtiness through virtual CPU and page accounting for writable entries, releases pinned references, and nulls stored handles.

Scratch negotiation enforces non empty length, presence and overflow freedom of the guest address, separation of embedded shared buffer use from external guest memory use, containment within the shared area for embedded use, version and size ceilings plus kernel staging copy for external use, lifetime and writeback bookkeeping, and malformed input signaling on violation.
External scratch ceiling equals sixteen pages.
Exit response reporting stores a response category and companion detail into the shared exit info fields, offering malformed input and no action variants.

Pre execution processing for encrypted guests rejects invalid protected save areas, remembers host CPUs that have entered guests for selective flushing, installs the guest identifier, and requests identifier flush on control block or CPU change with fast path retention otherwise.
Communication address field helpers extract or replace a masked bit slice at a caller chosen position.

Model register page state path accepts only private or shared transitions with userspace handling enabled, delegates a single page conversion carrying encryption direction and small page size to userspace, preserves zeroed result for compatibility, and on completion validates the result before publishing success or error and resuming.
Mapping hypercall outcomes treat success and two recoverable errors as legitimate, and delegation to userspace is allowed only where the corresponding enable bit is set.

Batched page state handling scans from the resumed index, rejects misaligned or over advanced entries, degrades split huge ranges to small granularity, merges contiguous same operation entries into a single userspace delegation, advances guest visible progress after each batch, and distinguishes generic from invalid entry failures with idle completion.

Unsafe inputs including user addresses for flush, wrapped or missing scratch addresses, oversize or misplaced scratch, version mismatch for external scratch, and misaligned page state ranges are contained through fallback flushing or explicit error responses.

Communication teardown for exits resets processor hold state, optionally writes back staged external data to guest memory, records an exit trace, publishes outward registers, and frees staging plus mapping resources, ignoring absent mappings.

Virtual CPU teardown for protected guests restores hypervisor ownership of secure save pages where applicable, flushes encrypted content while protection remains, frees the save page unless ownership transfer failed, and unconditionally releases communication resources, skipping legacy guests.
Pending secure initialization for a virtual CPU is indicated by a per virtual machine flag.
Table split support aligns the target frame to huge page start and repeats the operation while another processor reports the entry busy.
Generic host unmap service offers idempotent cleanup of per virtual CPU host mappings.

Diagnostic snapshot logging for failed communication exits is suppressed unless a debug control is enabled, and on enable reports the guest address plus hypervisor observed exit fields with validity and the validity bitmap.
